title: A relative which-ceedling path and vendor/ceedling are resolved from the working directory
claim: Verdict: kept. The selector checks `vendor/ceedling` and the configured path with `directory?`, which reads relative to the working directory. It never uses the project file's directory.

title: A symlink to the running installation is the same installation
claim: Verdict: kept. `Installation#identity` returns `File.realpath(@root)`, so two spellings of one directory compare equal.

title: A relative release :output is linked below build/release and copied flat into artifacts/release
claim: Verdict: partly kept. The docs say the artifact "is to be found in <build path>/artifacts/release/". With `:output: sub/app.out` the linker output is `build/release/sub/app.out`, and `artifactinate` copies it to `build/artifacts/release/app.out` without the `sub/`. The default name `project.out` is also copied there. `:artifacts` entries are copied to the same directory.

title: An absolute or ~ release :output names the release itself
claim: Verdict: kept. `release_place` keeps an absolute name as written and joins any other below the release root. `~` is expanded by `ProjectPaths.standardize`. Builds with an absolute `:output` and a `~/...` `:output` linked to those paths and still copied to `build/artifacts/release/app.out`.

title: The release-build doc example names build/release/out/c/, which the layout does not use
claim: Verdict: broken (illustrative). The `:artifacts` example is `build/release/out/c/top_secret.s19`. Release objects sit at `build/release/out/<source directory>/<name>.o` (`build/release/out/src/main.o`, `.../src/drv/led.o`). No `c/` directory exists.

title: The :extension lists name output files by their first entry
claim: Verdict: partly kept. Each type accepts a list and Ceedling collects files under any of them. Derived output names (objects, dependency files, maps) use `.primary`, the first entry, so a second entry never names an output.

title: Unity runner :includes entries are written to the runner as typed
claim: Verdict: kept. With `:test_runner` ↳ `:includes: [foo.h, sub/missing.h]` the runner holds `#include "foo.h"` and `#include "sub/missing.h"`, and the compiler finds both through the `:include` path.

title: The ${5} search path list holds more than the :paths and path-macro entries the tools doc names
claim: Verdict: partly kept. The doc says `-I"${5}"` expands to the search paths of `:paths` plus build directive path macros. The real test compile line puts the test's mocks root, Partials roots and each Partial subdirectory first, then `:include` entries, then the vendor roots. `:paths` ↳ `:test` and ↳ `:source` directories are not on it.

title: The tools doc's compile and link examples show a layout Ceedling does not build
claim: Verdict: broken (illustrative). The example compile line has `-I"project/tests" -I"project/source"` and outputs `build/tests/out/source.o`. The linker example writes `build\tests\out\test_thing.exe`. Ceedling builds objects at `build/test/out/<test path>/_t_/<mirrored source path>.o`. Source and test directories are not `-I` entries.

title: A tool executable written as a path is checked on disk and a bare name in the system search path
claim: Verdict: kept. `explicit_path?` is true when the executable holds `/` or `\`. Such a name is checked as a file relative to the working directory. A bare name is looked for in the system search paths.
